content.intro: Learn working with generic class-based views through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines working with generic class-based views as part of url routing and views. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: TemplateView; ListView; DetailView; CreateView; UpdateView and DeleteView. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: TemplateView
items.text: TemplateView shapes the presentation layer. Separate layout from business logic, escape untrusted output, provide meaningful empty/error states, and check semantic structure and keyboard usability.

items.title: ListView
items.text: ListView is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Working with Generic Class-Based Views
content_blocks.code:
from django.views.generic import ListView
from .models import Book

class BookListView(ListView):
    model = Book
    template_name = "catalog/book_list.html"
    context_object_name = "books"
content_blocks.expected_output: ListView queries Book objects and supplies them under the context name books to the configured template.

If this snippet depends on model names, URL configuration, settings, or an optional package, add those prerequisites before running it. Otherwise inspect it as a static example. CodeLeaf browser preview does not execute Django/Python server code.
content_blocks.troubleshooting: Add a URL pattern that calls BookListView.as_view(). Add pagination for large collections.
